decisions.decision: sslyze declared in core dependencies rather than the [email] extras group
decisions.rationale: Matches operators-guide's long-standing (until then false) 'sslyze (core)' claim for the TLS row; a bare install was silently running the flagship TLS scanner on its stdlib fallback with no error.

decisions.decision: New multihost services are dedicated mh-* instances with no published ports, not dual-homed existing services
decisions.rationale: Dual-homing would make hosts reachable both from the host and inside the subnet, eroding the topology exercise — and would have inherited samba-dc's published :88, which collides with the KDC macOS itself runs.
[Unreleased] already holds scoring v3; cutting a version would release a scoring overhaul as a side effect of a dependency fix.

decisions.decision: PRs #31 and #32 kept separate rather than combined
decisions.rationale: #31 stays a clean dependency fix. Cost is the stacked-PR retarget hazard, which STEP 1 handles explicitly.

decisions.decision: DNSSEC / S-MIME / AD CS multihost hosts not started
decisions.rationale: Each needs wiring beyond a static IP (resolver config, LDAP search bases, seeded certs). Half-landing three unknowns into a working lab hours before a demo was the wrong trade.

Do not assume GitHub retargeted it — it auto-retargets only when the base branch is deleted on merge, and this exact trap cost a stacked PR at the v5.23 close.
context_notes: The demo is over and went well; the time pressure that shaped the last few days is gone. The four-step order is deliberate: steps 1-2 restore trust in the merge pipeline (nine fixes stranded behind a stacked PR, and a CI signal nobody can read), and only then does resuming Phase 206 make sense — its eventual PR lands into the same pipeline otherwise. The through-line of every demo-prep finding: four separate defects were the same shape, something that works on every maintainer machine and fails on a clean host (undeclared sslyze, a Kerberos profile skipped on macOS so nobody ran it, an amd64-only image Docker Desktop emulates silently, a JWT connector blocked against exactly the private addresses every lab uses). The operator's clean aarch64 Linux VM is the most valuable test surface this project has gained in a while. Compiled view: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/ea676963-6c66-46e9-a90d-cca89726537e
